definitions.sequence: accounting records every guest call in order; array IDs are constructor order per fresh session; push arguments are deterministic item indices
definitions.comparisons: observed global deltas: one increment per non-null record visited by allocator FIND or per-type authority LOOKUP; includes all nested searches in the operation, not just one public helper; host loads execute no searches
definitions.capacity: full acquired power-of-two payload bytes, minimum 8; capacityElements sums per-array capacity divided by its element width; free capacity is untyped bytes
definitions.cumulative: sum over successful constructor/relocation acquisitions including reuse; copied live bytes inferred from verified relocations and pre-operation length times width, not measured memory-load/store counts; constructor copy bytes excluded
definitions.peaks: maxima at completed guest-operation boundaries only, not transient acquire-before-release high-water marks
definitions.backing: cursor minus fresh-instance initial cursor; includes allocator records, payloads, retained 48-byte authority objects, and other bump storage (constructor fixed literals/alignment); pages are total committed Wasm memory pages
definitions.parity: fresh ordinary and observed instances execute identical sequence; equal handles, public contents, returned scalars, pages and every initialized allocator/authority record; ordinary registry roots/cursor inferred from paired observed addresses, not independently exported

limitations: Private fixture layouts, not a public introspection or management ABI; trusted-host loads only.
No spare/free payload bytes are decoded or compared. This harness does not prove the absence of guest spare-byte loads; decoded lowering tests own that claim.
Disjointness covers full allocator record/payload and retained descriptor/authority extents, not a census of fixed literals/static string storage.
Peaks omit intra-operation transient double-capacity residency; no general reclamation, unreachable-array collection, trap rollback, or heap plateau claim.
Free-chain reconstruction verifies links and membership without exported class heads; it cannot independently verify hidden head globals.

Timing is ordinary-module host-driven execution, includes JS overhead and Wasm tiering/GC/system noise; no native execution or compiler-time inference, statistical significance, or release acceptance claim.

results.warmup: one full untimed case per type/kind on separate discarded ordinary instances
results.boundary: hrtime around JS operation loop, JS/Wasm calls, guest parameter validation, item selection, authority/allocator searches, mutation, allocation/copy/growth if needed, and returned scalar transport (ignored by timed loop); excludes compilation, instantiation, setup, oracle construction, decoding, assertions, and hashing

operations.append: 512 push calls from empty; includes geometric transitions
operations.spare-push-pop: 4096 push/pop pairs from empty with 128 elements reserved
operations.ordered-remove-push: 2048 remove/push pairs at constant length 64; remove indices cycle 0,32,63
operations.reserve-noop-oldest-32: 4096 reserve calls alternating additional 0/1 on oldest of 32 arrays; selected empty array has 128 elements reserved
